Rashi on Niddah 47a:10:1.hebrew: בזו ובזו - אפי' כשהיא נערה, אביה זכאי כו', דכתיב (במדבר ל׳:י״ז) בנעוריה בית אביה - כל שבח נעוריה לאביה:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:10:1.english: In both this and that - Even when she is a young woman [na'arah], her father is entitled, etc., as it is written (Numbers 30:17): "In her youth, in her father's house" — all profit of her youth [belongs] to her father.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:1.english: What are the signs - It refers to *tzemel* [a ripe fig, i.e., grown womanhood].

Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:2.english: A fold - Fronces [in Old French, wrinkles]. That her breasts have grown until [the breast] is slightly folded over the chest and appears like a fold.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:3.english: From when they incline - [The breasts are] even larger.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:4.hebrew: הפיטומת - ראש הדד, כמו (סוכה דף לד:) ניטלה פיטמתו:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:4.english: The pitomet - The tip of the breast, as in (Sukkah 34b): "Its pitma was removed."

Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:5.hebrew: עוקץ - כמו עוקצי האגסים (עוקצין פ"א מ"ו), פוכיצ"ש בלע"ז. חודו של דד שהתינוק יונק, ופיטומת היינו סביבות עוקץ:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:11:5.english: A stalk [oketz] - Like "the stalks of pears" (Uktzin 1:6); poinçon in Old French. The tip of the breast from which the infant nurses; and pitomet refers to the surroundings of the stalk [i.e., the areola].

Rashi on Niddah 47a:12:1.english: From when they begin to ripen - [They are] obligated in tithes.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:12:2.english: From when their heads whiten - That they change as they grow. Here too, from when the breast changes and a sign is visible in it that it is growing.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:13:1.english: Loathed Me - It grew large upon Me. A person who loathes something, it appears to him as large. Anquaisance in Old French.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:16:1.hebrew: מייחד להו - שפחותיו מייחד לאנשים עבדיו, ואינו מפקירן משום בושת:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:16:1.english: Would designate for them - He would designate his maidservants for [specific] men, his male slaves, and would not treat them as ownerless, out of concern for [their] shame.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:16:2.hebrew: מחליף להן - את של זה בזה, ואינו מקפיד על בושתן:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:16:2.english: Would exchange for them - The [maidservant] of this one for that one, and he was not concerned about their humiliation.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:16:3.english: To an Arab - He would abandon his maidservants to Arabs and treat them in the manner of ownerless property.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:18:1.hebrew: משיתקשקשו - כמו (סוטה דף ט:) מקשקשת לפניו כזוג, בטנ"ט בלע"ז. כלומר: גדולים הרבה:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:18:1.english: From when they knock against each other - As in (Sotah 9b): "[The Divine Presence was] ringing before him like a bell," batant in Old French. That is to say, [they are] very large.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:18:2.english: The nose - [This is a matter of] halakhic uncertainty regarding the case.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:18:3.english: From when it splits - [This is a case of] halakhic doubt [an uncertain status regarding her maturity].

Rashi on Niddah 47a:18:4.hebrew: משתקיף עטרה - שגדול העוקץ ועב, ומוקף עטרה. והיינו שיעורא דא"ר יוסי נמי במתני', שיהא נותן ידו על העוקץ, ושוקע ושוהא לחזור:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:18:4.english: From when a crown surrounds [it] - That the nipple is large and thick, and surrounded by a crown [i.e., an areola]. And this is the measure that Rabbi Yosei stated in the mishna as well: that one places his hand on the nipple, and it depresses and is slow to return.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:1:1.hebrew: חייבת בחלה - ולא אמרינן דתרומה פוטרת לה. ואע"ג דתרומה אינה חייבת בחלה, מדומע חייב בחלה. מ"ט? דדימוע דרבנן הוא, דמדאורייתא חד בתרי בטיל, דכתיב (שמות כ״ג:ב׳) אחרי רבים להטות, ורבנן הוא דאצרוך אחד ומאה. הלכך לא אתי דימוע דרבנן ומפקע חלה, אפילו בזמן הזה, דקסברי ר"מ ורבי יהודה: חלה בזמן הזה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:1:1.english: Obligated in challah - And we do not say that the terumah exempts it. And even though terumah is not obligated in challah, meduma [dough mixed with terumah] is obligated in challah. What is the reason? Because [the status of] dimua is rabbinic, for by Torah law, one [part] is nullified in two [i.e., by a simple majority], as it is written (Exodus 23:2): "After the majority to incline," and it was the Rabbis who required one [part to] one hundred. Therefore, rabbinic dimua does not come and abrogate [the obligation of] challah, even in the present era, as Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda hold that challah in the present era is [an obligation] by Torah law.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:1:2.hebrew: פוטרין מן החלה - כדמפרש לקמן, דקסברי: חלה בזמן הזה דרבנן, ואתי דימוע דרבנן ומפקע חלה דרבנן. והיינו דאמרן לעיל: תני ולא סבר לה, דהא חזינן דלרבי יוסי חלה בזמן הזה דרבנן. וסברוה הנך רבנן דמייתי ראייה מהכא, דכי היכי דקאמר ר' יוסי חלה בזמן הזה דרבנן, הוא הדין לתרומה:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:1:2.english: Exempt from challah - As [the Gemara] explains below, that they maintain that challah in the present time is rabbinic, and a rabbinic mixture [with teruma] comes and abrogates rabbinic challah. And this is what we said above: "[Rabbi Yosei] taught [it], but did not hold by it," for behold, we see that according to Rabbi Yosei, challah in the present time is rabbinic; and those Rabbis who brought a proof from here reasoned that just as Rabbi Yosei says challah in the present time is rabbinic, the same applies to teruma.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:4:1.hebrew: ודלמא - אע"ג דקא חזית מהכא לר' יוסי חלה דרבנן, אפ"ה סבירא ליה תרומה דאורייתא, וליכא הכי נמי מסתברא דקא בעית לאתויי:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:4:1.english: And perhaps - Even though you see from here that according to Rabbi Yosei, challah is rabbinic, even so, he maintains that terumah is by Torah law, and there is no [proof from] "so too, it is reasonable" that you sought to bring.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:6:1.hebrew: נתחייבו בחלה - דכתיב בחלה (במדבר ט״ו:י״ח) בבואכם אל הארץ, והרי באו:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:6:1.english: They were obligated in challah - For it is written regarding challah (Numbers 15:18): "When you come into the land," and behold, they had come.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:6:2.hebrew: ולא נתחייבו במעשר - דבמעשר כתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ב) תבואת זרעך, עד שיביא כל אחד ואחד את שלו:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:6:2.english: And they were not obligated in tithe - For regarding tithe it is written (Deuteronomy 14:22): "The produce of your seed," [meaning that they are not obligated] until each and every one brings his own [produce].

Rashi on Niddah 47a:9:1.hebrew: פגה - סמדר. כך באשה: עודה תינוקת, קרו לה פגה, כל זמן שאין לה סימן, לא בדדים ולא בשערות:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:9:1.english: An unripe fig - [An early budding fruit, like] semadar. So too regarding a woman: while she is still a child, they call her an unripe fig [paga], as long as she has no sign [of puberty], neither in the breasts nor in [pubic] hairs.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:9:2.hebrew: בוחל - כשהפרי גדל קצת, כדתני בגמרא התאנים משיבחלו. כך, כשיש לה סימן דדין קצת, בידוע שהביאה שתי שערות, ונערה היא:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:9:2.english: A ripening fig - When the fruit has grown a little, as is taught in the Gemara: "The figs from when they begin to ripen." So too, when she has a slight sign of breasts, it is known that she has produced two hairs, and she is a young woman.

Rashi on Niddah 47a:9:3.hebrew: צמל - בגמ' מפרש לה לשון נוטריקון: "יצתה מלאה", שיש לה סימן מובהק בדדיה, ולקמן מפרש סימנין במתני'. והיא בוגרת:
Rashi on Niddah 47a:9:3.english: A fully ripe fig [tzemel] - In the Gemara, it explains it as an acronym: "She has emerged full" [yatzetah mele'ah], meaning that she has a prominent sign on her breasts; and later, the signs are explained in the mishna. And she is a bogeret [a mature woman].

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:11:1.hebrew: איזהו סימניה - פ"ה: סימני בגרות. ורבי יוסי דאמר בגמרא "משתקיף העטרה", היינו נמי דקאמר הכא "משיתן ידו על העוקץ". וקשה: דאי חד שיעורא הוא, למה שינה רבי יוסי לשונו? ותו, דכל תנאי דגמרא, שום אחד מהם אינו מזכיר משיעורא דמתניתין. ועוד, דאם כן, בבוחל לא נתן שום סימן; ובגמרא קאמר: "בוחל מלמעלה — בידוע שהביאה ב' שערות", הא לא שמעינן סימני דבוחל! לכך פר"ת, ד"איזהו סימניה" דקאמר הכא — אבוחל קאי. ולפירוש זה אתי שפיר הא דקאמר בגמרא: "הלכה כדברי כולן להחמיר", לענין מיאון:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:11:1.english: What are her signs? - Rashi explained: The signs of maturity (bagrut). And Rabbi Yosei, who said in the Gemara, "From when the areola surrounds [the nipple]," is also [saying the same as] that which he said here [in the Mishnah], "From when one places his hand on the nipple." And this is difficult: for if it is one [and the same] measure, why did Rabbi Yosei change his wording? And furthermore, of all the Tannaim in the Gemara, not one of them mentions [any] of the measures of the Mishnah. And furthermore, if so, [the Tanna] gave no sign at all for a ripening girl (bochel); yet in the Gemara it says: "[If she is] a bochel above, it is known that she has brought two hairs" — yet we have not heard [taught] the signs of a bochel! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that "What are her signs?" which it states here refers to a bochel. And according to this explanation, that which is stated in the Gemara, "The halakha is in accordance with the words of all of them to be stringent," works out well regarding the matter of refusal (mi'un).

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:15:1.hebrew: בדק באמתיה ויהיב ד' זוזי דמי בושתה - להנצל מעונש היה נותן לה, דהא ר' יהודה אמר בהחובל (ב"ק דף פז.) אין לעבדים בושת; ואפילו למ"ד יש לעבדים בושת, הוי לרבו:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:15:1.english: He examined his maidservant and gave four zuz [as] compensation for her embarrassment - He gave [it] to her [in order] to be spared from [divine] punishment, for Rabbi Yehudah said in [chapter] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 87a), "Slaves have no [claim to] embarrassment"; and even according to the one who says slaves do have [a claim to] embarrassment, it belongs to their master.

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:16:1.hebrew: מסר להו לערבי - משמע מכאן דשפחה כנענית מותרת בעובד כוכבים, וה"ה דעבד כנעני מותר בעובדת כוכבים, ולא גזרו עליו משום נשג"ז, אע"ג דאיסור נדה ואשת איש דאורייתא שייך שפיר בעבד. וא"כ, בשלהי מסכת ע"ז (דף עו:), דא"ל שבור מלכא לבטי: אדכר לך מה דעבדת באורתא — שקבל עובדת כוכבים זונה שמסר לו אושפיזו, (ורב) יהודה לא קבל עובדת כוכבים זונה — לא עשה בטי איסורא, דמותר הוה בה, דהא עבד הוה; כדקאמר בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף ע:), דבטי בר טבי ברמות רוחיה לא קבל גיטא דחירותא:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:16:1.english: He handed them over to an Arab - It is implied from here that a Canaanite maidservant is permitted to a gentile, and the same applies to a Canaanite manservant, that he is permitted to a gentile woman; and they did not decree against him on account of NaShaGZ [the rabbinic prohibitions of a menstruant (niddah), a maidservant (shifchah), a gentile (goyah), and a harlot (zonah)], even though the biblical prohibition of a menstruant (niddah) and a married woman (eshet ish) certainly applies to a slave. And if so, at the end of Tractate Avodah Zarah (daf 76b), where King Shapur said to Bati: "Remember what you did last night" — in that he accepted a gentile prostitute whom his host had provided to him, while (Rav) Yehuda did not accept a gentile prostitute — Bati did not commit a transgression, for he was permitted to her, since he was a slave, as [the Gemara] says in chapter Asarah Yuḥasin (Kiddushin daf 70b), that Bati bar Tovi, out of his arrogance, did not accept a bill of manumission.

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:18:1.hebrew: ראש החוטם - פ"ה: ספק, דלא אתפרש. ובפרק לולב הגזול (סוכה דף לה:), גבי אתרוג, מזכיר פיטומא ועוקץ וחוטם; ומתוך כך משמע דשלשתן באתרוג לצד ראשו, ואין אחד מהם לצד זנבו, דומיא דדד — דגבי דד ליכא לפרושי הכי, כמו שפירש באתרוג:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:18:1.english: The head of the protrusion - Rashi explained: “[Its meaning is in] doubt,” for it was not explained. And in chapter Lulav HaGazul (Sukkah 35b), regarding an etrog, [the Gemara] mentions [its] pituma [blossom protrusion], oketz [stalk], and chotem [nose-like protrusion]; and from this it implies that all three of them in an etrog are toward its head, and not one of them is toward its tail, analogous to a breast — for regarding a breast, it is impossible to explain it as [Rashi] explained regarding an etrog.

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:1:1.hebrew: ואינה נפסלת בטבול יום - וא"ת: באלו עוברין (פסחים דף מד.), גבי מקפה של חולין ושום ושמן של תרומה, קאמר דאם נגע טבול יום במקצתו דפסל כולו במגעו; וי"ל, דהתם מיירי בשעשאו גוש בקערה:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:1:1.english: And it is not disqualified by one who immersed that day - And if you say: In [the chapter] "Elu Overin" (Pesachim 44a), regarding a thick soup of non-sacred food (chullin) and garlic and oil of teruma, it says that if one who immersed that day (tevul yom) touched part of it, he disqualifies all of it through his touch? And one can say that there, it is dealing with [a case where] they made it [into] a lump in the bowl.

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:2:1.hebrew: אתי דימוע דרבנן ומפקע חלה דרבנן - מכאן מביא ריב"א ראיה דתרומה בטלה ברוב דאורייתא. והא דדרשינן בסיפרא מאת מקדשו ממנו דעולה בק"א, אסמכתא בעלמא הוא; וכן הא דקאמר התם: דערלה וכלאי הכרם דכפל איסורו ליאסר בהנאה כפל בעלייתו שצריך אחד ומאתים. ומיהו, ראייה דהכא יש לדחות: דלעולם מדאורייתא הכל נאסר לזרים מטעם תערובת התרומה שאינה ניכר; אבל מה שגם החולין נחשבו כתרומה ליפטר מן החלה כאילו הכל תרומה, זה אינו אלא מדרבנן. ומיהו, יש להביא ראיה גבי נפלו אגוזים ונתפצעו בהניזקין (גיטין דף נד:), דיש ספרים דגרסי: והא הכא דמדאוריית' ברובו בטלה. ובשלהי הערל (יבמות דף פב.) גבי שתי קופות, אחת של חולין ואחת של תרומה, ולפניהן שתי סאות כו', דקא"ר יוחנן: והוא שרבו חולין על התרומה, פי' דשרי מדאורייתא, ולהכי אמר שאני אומר. ובריש ההוא פירקא (דף עג:) נמי קאמר: תרומה חמורה ממעשר שכן מחפ"ז, ולא חשיב ק"א:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:2:1.english: A rabbinic dimmu'a [mixture of terumah] comes and abrogates rabbinic challah - From here, the Riva brings proof that terumah is nullified in a majority by Torah law. And that which we expound in the Sifra, "out of it even the hallowed part thereof" (Numbers 18:29), that it is neutralized in one hundred and one [parts], is a mere asmachta (scriptural support); and likewise that which it says there: that regarding orlah and diverse seeds of the vineyard (kil'ei hakerem), whose prohibition is doubled [in that it is] prohibited from benefit, its [ratio for] neutralization is doubled, such that it requires one and two hundred [parts]. However, the proof from here can be refuted: for in fact, by Torah law, everything becomes forbidden to non-priests (zarim) because of the mixture of terumah that is not discernible; but the fact that the chullin is also considered like terumah to be exempt from challah, as though all of it were terumah — that is only rabbinic. However, one can bring proof from [the case of] nuts that fell and cracked open in [the chapter of] HaNizakin (Gittin 54b), where there are texts that read: "And yet here, by Torah law it is nullified in a majority;" and at the end of [the chapter of] HaArel (Yevamot 82a), regarding two baskets, one of chullin and one of terumah, and before them were two se'ahs, etc., where Rabbi Yochanan said: "And this is [only] when the chullin exceeded the terumah" — that is to say, that it is permitted by Torah law, and that is why he said: "I can say [that the terumah fell into the terumah]"; and at the beginning of that chapter (page 73b), it also says: "Terumah is more stringent than tithes, in that [its stringencies are abbreviated by the mnemonic] MaCHePaZ" [mitah (death at the hand of Heaven), chomesh (adding a fifth), pidyon (it cannot be redeemed), and zarut (forbidden to non-priests)], and it does not reckon one hundred and one [parts].

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:7:1.hebrew: ל"ג אילו נאמר כי תבואו הייתי אומר משנכנסו ב' או ג' מרגלים - דהא רישא דברייתא הכי איתא בספרי (פרשת שלח) (ובספ"ק דקדושין מייתי לה): משונה ביאה זו של חלה, דבעלמא כתיב כי תבואו כי יביאך, וכאן כתיב בבואכם, לומר: מיד כשנכנסו, קודם כבוש וחילוק. אלמא משמע דכי תבואו משמע ביאה חשובה, דהיינו לאחר כבוש וחילוק; והיכי מצי למימר אפי' ב' או ג' מרגלים? אלא הכי גרסינן: אי בבואכם יכול אפי' ב' או ג' מרגלים, וקאי אדלעיל מיניה:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:7:1.english: We do not read: "Had it been stated: 'When you come,' I would have said: From [the time] that two or three spies entered" - For the beginning of the baraita is stated as follows in the Sifrei (Parashat Shelach) (and at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin [37b], it cites it): "This entry [regarding the mitzvah] of challah is different, for elsewhere it is written: 'When you come' (ki tavo'u) [or] 'When He brings you' (ki yevi'akha), whereas here it is written: 'When you come' (be-vo'akhem) — to say: Immediately when they entered, prior to conquest and division." It is implied, therefore, that "When you come" signifies a significant entry, which is after conquest and division; how, then, could it say: "even two or three spies"? Rather, this is the correct text: "If [it says] 'When you come' (be-vo'akhem), one might think even [from when] two or three spies [entered]?" And it refers to that which is above it.

Tosafot on Niddah 47a:8:1.hebrew: לא כולהו סלוק - ואם תאמר: והלא כל יושביה עליה קרינן לענין יובל, לפי שמקצת כל השבטים עלו, לפר"ת דאמר דיובל נהג בבית שני מהאי טעמא? וי"ל, דבבואכם משמע טפי בביאת כולכם. ואם תאמר: היכי ס"ד מעיקרא דתרומה בזמן הזה דאורייתא לרבי יוסי, והוי סייעתא לר"ל דלעיל? הא ר"ל גופיה סבר דלר' יוסי תרומה בזמן הזה דרבנן, בפרק הערל (יבמות ד' פא.)! וי"ל, דהוי מצי למימר וליטעמיך:
Tosafot on Niddah 47a:8:1.english: Not all of them ascended - And if you say: But do we not read [the requirement of] "all its inhabitants upon it" regarding the Jubilee because some of each of the tribes ascended, according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, who said that the Jubilee was practiced in the Second Temple for this reason? And one can say that "when you come" (bevo'akhem) implies more [strictly] the arrival of all of you. And if you say: How could it enter your mind initially that according to Rabbi Yosei, terumah in the present is [by] Torah law, and [that] this was a support for Reish Lakish above? Behold, Reish Lakish himself held that according to Rabbi Yosei, terumah in the present is rabbinic, in chapter HaArel (Yevamot 81a)! And one can say that he could have said: "And according to your reasoning" (u-le-ta'ameikh) [i.e., even according to your premise that terumah is by Torah law, this supports Reish Lakish].
